subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different kinds of hardware problems appear in these incidents?

judge.implied_focus: Hardware problem type/failure characterization in incidents

per_column.name: hardware_failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Directly categorizes the kind of hardware failure (connectivity, power, overheating, physical damage), which is the core of 'kinds of hardware problems'.

per_column.name: affected_device_scope
per_column.rationale: Identifies which hardware device class is affected, a coherent facet distinguishing types of hardware problems by their locus.

per_column.name: hardware_problem_involves_replacement
per_column.rationale: A remediation/severity attribute of the hardware problem; coherent with the focus though nearly constant (597 false / 3 true), so of limited discriminative value.

judge.rationale: All three columns cluster tightly on one inferable focus -- characterizing hardware problems in incidents -- rather than a grab-bag, giving high coherence. The structure offers two complementary, well-differentiated facets (failure mode = what went wrong; device scope = what hardware) at a useful granularity, plus a remediation attribute. This is a sound predictor/attribute set for the query. Structure is docked slightly because the replacement flag is almost degenerate (99.5% false) and adds little analytical differentiation, and both categorical columns carry heavy NULL rates. The implied focus is genuinely actionable: an analyst can profile failure-mode distributions across device classes to prioritize investigation, so actionability is high.
